title: Learned light-curve templates date the observed phase of supernova Ares
summary: Gaussian-process light-curve templates estimated that the JWST spectrum of the lensed Type IIb supernova Ares was taken about 34 rest-frame days after peak brightness, with a reported 25–44 day interval. Fits to three nearby analogues gave similar estimates. The source’s classification and predicted future images came from separate spectroscopic and lens-model analyses.
organization: Space Telescope Science Institute; Johns Hopkins University; University of Texas at Austin; Chiba University; University of Toronto; Princeton University

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 front matter, Section V.2 Gaussian-process template learning and phase fit, spectroscopic cross-check

evidence.tested: The study fit photometry to three nearby Type IIb supernova templates and a population template. Its phase estimates were consistent with spectral comparisons within uncertainty.
evidence.unknown: The analysis covers one event. Population and individual templates share source observations, and spectroscopic estimates informed phase priors.
evidence.ai_role: Gaussian-process regression inferred continuous light-curve templates from observed local Type IIb supernovae. The astronomy team fitted SN Ares photometry to these learned templates.
